incident-bot: PagerDuty PAGER FIRED for cluster solaris-reserved-42 — metrics: reserved_pool_latency_p95 > 500ms for 3m, reserved_pool_5xx_rate > 2% for 2m. Trigger: reserved-pool-latency-alert rule.
Alex P: acked — I'm oncall, opening a short bridge. @Priya S can you triage? :rotating_light:
Priya S: looking now. I can see a big spike in KV cache miss rate and backend GPU queue depth. Top error is 'kv_fetch_timeout' from the kv-proxy. Token counts per request look normal. Trying to correlate with autoscaler events.
Sam R: adding runtime view — batching backlog climbed to ~2200 concurrent reqs (target 1000). Worker threads are saturated, long queue wait times. Might be autoscaler or node provisioning lag.
Priya S: running quick checks. Here's a snippet of what I'm seeing in metrics explorer:
```
series: reserved_pool.queue_length{cluster="solaris-reserved-42"} -> 2200
series: reserved_pool.kv_miss_rate{cluster="solaris-reserved-42"} -> 18%
series: reserved_pool.node_ready{cluster="solaris-reserved-42"} -> 3 nodes
```
Priya S: autoscaler didn't add nodes — headroom flag is currently 0. Pushing a quick config patch to allow emergency scale-up.
Priya S: running commands to scale now:
```sh
# inspect pool
rcli pool get solaris-reserved-42 --metrics
# emergency bump +2 GPUs
rcli pool scale --id solaris-reserved-42 --delta=+2 --reason="oncall emergency scale - kv miss spike"
```
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: Alex P acknowledged at 5187654325. If unresolved escalate to level-2 in 8m.
Jen C: I've pinged Customer Success and left a short customer-facing blurb in the incident doc: "We're investigating elevated latency on your dedicated pool; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15m."
PagerDuty: Level-2 escalation scheduled. Note: automated escalation to L2 if not resolved by 5187654805.
incident-bot: Autoscaler event: initiated node provisioning, 2 nodes requested for solaris-reserved-42 (ETA ~90s).
Alex P: while nodes come up I'm going to apply a temporary routing override to send high-priority interactive traffic to a low-latency fallback model variant to reduce pressure on the pool. Applying override now.
Sam R: enabling aggressive prefix caching for this tenant to cut KV lookups; toggling tenant-specific cache mode = aggressive.
Priya S: patch applied to pool config: headroom_pct=15 (was 0). Confirmed config rolled to 3 control-plane replicas.
incident-bot: node(s) added: 2 new GPU nodes joined solaris-reserved-42; scheduler placing pods.
Alex P: traffic reroute applied: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-lite-3.7b","policy":"fallback-solaris-2026-03-15"}
```
Alex P: monitoring — p95 dropped from ~560ms -> ~220ms within 2m after nodes ready and routing change. Error rate down from 2.6% -> 0.4%.
Priya S: confirming KV miss rate dropping as prefix cache warms: 18% -> 4% in last minute. Looks like autoscale + cache did the trick.
Jen C: SolarisOps (customer) DM: "We were seeing 503s — appreciate the quick action, keep us posted." I've added that to the incident timeline.
PagerDuty: Incident escalated to L2 and acknowledged by Priya S at 5187654440.
Sam R: creating a follow-up runbook todo: add unit/integration test for autoscaler headroom=0 edge-case; add alert that flags headroom==0 for reserved pools.
Alex P: good catch. I'll stay on bridge for the next 30m for observation. If things are stable handoff to Priya for post-incident cleanup and RCA.
Priya S: will take post-incident tasks and own RCA. Initial hypothesis: headroom misconfig prevented autoscaler from reacting quickly; combined with transient KV proxy latency spike.
Alex P: closing action items: 1) confirm autoscaler health checks & metrics alarm, 2) route fallback evaluates within 60s, 3) customer comms follow-up (Jen).
Jen C: I'll send the customer update and sync with success ops.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated — p95 within SLO for 3 consecutive samples. Bridge will remain open for monitoring; please update incident doc with timestamps.
Alex P: handoff to Priya S for RCA and follow-up. Leaving bridge at 5187654570. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
